as_told.title: Brain waves used to guide ICBMs

plain: Philip J. Corso, an Army officer, claimed that in the 1950s he worked at the Pentagon handing out recovered UFO material to private companies, and that some of it was used to steer weapons with the mind. Michels sums up Corso's claim this way, alongside the guest Dan Sheehan. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb adds detail from Corso's account. He says the Foreign Technology Division, a military unit that studied foreign weapons, tried to use recovered technology to let human brain waves guide intercontinental and other ballistic missiles, and he dates this to about 1958 to 1962. If true, it would mean crashed-craft technology went into American weapons.
